evals.name: rename-across-repo
evals.prompt: rename get_user to fetch_user across the repo
evals.expected_output: A complexity card with all seven scores, a low tier (haiku, or inline), no fan-out, tests run as the check, no verifier, and the decision logged with an id.
assertions: States all seven complexity scores (S, R, A, K, I, P, V) explicitly with values
The executing piece is inline or a haiku-tier agent, not sonnet/opus/fable
Does not fan out to multiple parallel agents
Names a deterministic acceptance check (zero-hit grep, compile, or tests) rather than a judgment review
No verifier agent and no human gate are added for this low-risk rename
The decision is recorded in a machine-readable log with an id (decisions.jsonl contains a decision line)

evals.name: intermittent-500s-checkout
evals.prompt: we're seeing intermittent 500s on /checkout under load. find the cause and fix it.
evals.expected_output: A card scoring reasoning high and risk at 2 (payments), an opus or fable tier, a scoping probe or explicit diagnosis step before the fix, an independent verifier, and a review gate rather than a direct deploy; diagnosis kept close to the user rather than blindly fanned out.
assertions: States all seven complexity scores (S, R, A, K, I, P, V) explicitly with values
The executing model for the diagnosis/fix is opus or fable (not haiku or sonnet)
Includes a scoping or diagnosis step before committing to a fix approach
Adds an independent verifier that receives the diff and the task but not the reasoning behind the fix
Names a review/merge gate and rules out a direct deploy, acknowledging the payments/data risk
Does not fan the diagnosis out to parallel agents
The decision is recorded in a machine-readable log with an id (decisions.jsonl contains a decision line)

evals.name: auth-audit-fan-out
evals.prompt: audit every route handler for missing auth checks and give me a report
evals.expected_output: A card with high parallelism and scope, a fan-out with a shard count and a fixed per-shard return schema, shards no cheaper than sonnet because auth is K2, an inline reduce, and an independent verifier on the merged report.
assertions: States all seven complexity scores (S, R, A, K, I, P, V) explicitly with values
No piece of the audit runs on haiku; the auditing model is sonnet or better because auth is risk 2
Adds an independent verifier for the report, aimed at catching confident false negatives
Specifies a fixed per-handler return schema (columns such as handler, file:line, auth present, evidence)
Sizes the repo (counts handlers or route modules) before choosing between fan-out and a single agent
The fan-out vs single-agent choice is stated with a reason tied to shard size or independence
The decision is recorded in a machine-readable log with an id (decisions.jsonl contains a decision line)
